original_question: Determine whether quasi-plurisubharmonic functions can be desingularized in every complex dimension n >= 3 in the same sense known in dimensions at most 2, namely after suitable blow-ups separating divisorial singularities from a residual positive current with arbitrarily small Lelong numbers.
target_in_paper: Section 5.1, Question 34 (Favre-Guedj-Jonsson): the open problem asking whether one can desingularize quasi-plurisubharmonic functions in all complex dimensions n >= 3 in the same way known for dim_C X <= 2.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact open problem in the paper: it is about quasi-plurisubharmonic functions, asks for an extension from the known case dim_C X <= 2 to all dimensions n >= 3, and correctly describes the intended desingularization mechanism via blow-ups that separate a divisorial part from a residual positive current with arbitrarily small Lelong numbers.
missing_details: The ambient space in the paper is a compact complex Hermitian manifold (X, omega), not an arbitrary complex manifold or a purely local setting.
The object being desingularized is a quasi-psh function varphi with the associated positive current T := omega + dd^c varphi >= 0.
The paper formulates the statement in terms of the pulled-back current pi_epsilon^*(omega + dd^c varphi), not just the function varphi abstractly.
The quantifier is explicit: for every epsilon > 0, there should exist a finite composition of blow-ups pi_epsilon : X_epsilon -> X.
The divisorial term is required to be [D_epsilon], where D_epsilon is a simple normal crossing divisor with coefficients in R_+.
The residual term R_epsilon must be a positive (1,1)-current whose Lelong numbers satisfy nu(R_epsilon, x) < epsilon for every point x in X_epsilon.
The paper frames the question as an analogue of a precise known result when dim_C X <= 2, not as a vague desingularization principle.

The nearby context also records a weaker decomposition valid in all dimensions, omega + dd^c varphi = sum_j m_j [D_j] + R, where E_+(R) contains no divisor but may still contain infinitely many analytic subsets of codimension >= 2; the open problem asks for the stronger blow-up refinement beyond this.
Your draft does not mention that the blow-ups are finite compositions of blow-ups, which is part of the exact formulation.
refined_question:
Let (X, omega) be a compact complex Hermitian manifold of complex dimension n >= 3, and let varphi be a quasi-plurisubharmonic function on X such that T := omega + dd^c varphi is a positive closed (1,1)-current. Is it true that for every epsilon > 0 there exists a finite composition of blow-ups pi_epsilon : X_epsilon -> X such that
pi_epsilon^* T = [D_epsilon] + R_epsilon,
where [D_epsilon] is the current of integration along a simple normal crossing divisor D_epsilon with coefficients in R_+, and R_epsilon is a positive (1,1)-current satisfying nu(R_epsilon, x) < epsilon for all x in X_epsilon?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 5.1 rather than any earlier statement: the paper first sets up the general decomposition of omega + dd^c varphi into divisorial and residual parts, then states the stronger dimension <= 2 result with arbitrary epsilon > 0 after a finite sequence of blow-ups, and immediately asks in Question 34 whether one can 'similarly desingularize quasi-plurisubharmonic functions in any dimension n >= 3'. Your draft is therefore very close to the paper's exact intent, but it leaves implicit the Hermitian ambient data, the positivity assumption on omega + dd^c varphi, the exact pullback identity, the SNC and R_+ nature of the divisor, and the universal quantifier over epsilon.
